clue.text: Language almost dead, going by name

indicators.note: almost means the word for dead is not quite complete, losing its final letter

parts.note: dead means late, as in the late king
going by means via, by way of

explanation.surface: A tongue that is nearly extinct is identified by what it is called.
explanation.definitionFit: Latvian is the Baltic tongue spoken in Latvia, so it is a language.

clue.text: Group of French composers is short of nine

parts.note: short of means less, as in five less two
IX is nine in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A band of French composers turns out to have fewer than nine members.
explanation.walkthrough: Les Six were Poulenc, Milhaud, Honegger and three others, a 1920s Parisian circle.
explanation.definitionFit: The French composers' circle of the 1920s was known collectively by this name.

clue.text: See 24
Little information etc about debts likely to be spread

indicators.note: Little asks for a shortened form of the next word, its last letter dropped

parts.note: info is the everyday short form of information

indicators.note: about here means knocked about, so the letters of etc are rearranged

parts.note: IOUs are written acknowledgements of debts

explanation.surface: Gossip and so on about money owed tends to get around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little information' is info cut short; 'about' is the anagram signal for etc, not a container, and IOUs are written promises to repay.
explanation.definitionFit: Something infectious, like a disease or laughter, is readily passed on to others.

clue.text: SF writer's last two characters given a lead role — surely not!

indicators.text: last two characters given a lead role
indicators.note: the final pair of letters of the writer's name are moved to lead, at the front

parts.note: Jules Verne was a pioneering science-fiction writer

explanation.surface: A science-fiction author's minor characters being given the starring part seems unbelievable.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving NE from the end of VERNE to the front gives the exclamation; 'characters' means letters, not people in a story.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'never!' expresses disbelief, just as 'surely not!' does.

clue.text: Name an itchy eruption

indicators.note: an eruption throws things about, so the letters of an itchy are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone names an itchy rash on the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Cynthia is a woman's first name, so it is an example of a name.

clue.text: Terrible vice: six dropped aitches — give instruction

indicators.note: Terrible signals that the letters that remain are mangled into a new order
dropped means the letters for six are taken out of vice

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone dropping their aitches is denounced as a dreadful vice by a speech teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped' takes VI out of VICE, leaving CE; 'Terrible' then rearranges CE with AITCHES.
explanation.definitionFit: To catechise is to teach by question and answer, especially in religious instruction.

clue.text: Clout means nowt without one?

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so nil goes around the letter for one

parts.note: nowt is northern English for nothing, nil
A means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: Does hitting someone mean nothing without one?
explanation.definitionFit: A clout is a short flat-headed nail, so the definition is a specific type of it.

clue.text: Time of radioactive decline — 35?

definitions.meaning: the period over which half the atoms of a radioactive sample decay
half of the biblical life span of threescore years and ten, i.e. half of seventy

explanation.walkthrough: 35 looks like a cross-reference to another clue, but there is no 35; it is half of a proverbial 70-year life.
explanation.definitionFit: Physicists measure radioactive decay by the time taken for half the material to decay.

clue.text: Knowing mechanisms which are between an aqueduct's supports?

definitions.text: which are between an aqueduct's supports?

parts.note: arch as an adjective means knowing or roguish, as in an arch look
ways means means or mechanisms, ways of doing something

explanation.surface: Clever devices sit between the piers of a water-carrying bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: An aqueduct stands on piers with curved openings between them, each one a passage under an arch.

clue.text: Don't talk in front of a fairy's mantelpiece

indicators.note: in front of places the first piece before the next one

parts.note: sh is the command to be quiet
an elf is a fairy-like creature

explanation.surface: A warning to keep quiet in front of a fairy's fireplace.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantelpiece is a ledge above a fireplace, a kind of shelf.

clue.text: Mean (extremely so) of 3 into 5151 + 100

indicators.note: into means the group of three goes inside the numerals

parts.note: 5, 1, 50 and 1 as Roman numerals are V, I, L and I
a trio is a group of three
C is 100 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Arithmetic puzzle: what is three put into 5151 plus 100?
explanation.walkthrough: The numbers are read as Roman numerals: 5151 is V I L I.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitriolic speech is bitterly cruel, i.e. extremely mean or spiteful.

clue.text: Error in invoice associated with assistant clerical post

parts.note: a/c is short for account, a bill or invoice
a curacy is the office of a curate, an assistant to a vicar

explanation.surface: A mistake on a bill relating to an assistant priest's job.
explanation.definitionFit: An inaccuracy is a mistake or factual error.

clue.text: See 21
Digital cruncher seeks lift from team

parts.note: a hitchhiker thumbs a lift, signalling with the thumb
a crew is a team, as of rowers or workers

explanation.surface: A digit-crushing device needs a boost from the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digital' refers to fingers and thumbs, not computers.
explanation.definitionFit: A thumbscrew is a torture device that crushes the thumbs, which are digits.

clue.text: Sows at power speed? Highly unlikely

parts.note: sows are female pigs
might means power or strength
to fly is to speed along

explanation.surface: Female hogs racing at full power: hardly likely.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom expresses that something is so improbable it will never happen.

clue.text: Diminish in years, sadly becoming inactive

indicators.note: in places the word for diminish inside the rearranged letters
sadly signals that the letters of years are badly arranged

parts.note: to dent is to diminish, as in denting someone's confidence

explanation.surface: Getting sluggish as one ages, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diminish' looks like it acts on years, but it supplies a word of its own, which 'in' places inside the jumbled years.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedentary life involves a lot of sitting and little exercise, so it is inactive.

clue.text: Curry favour, centrally hosting laid-on spread

indicators.note: hosting means the central letters hold the rearranged letters inside them
centrally takes the middle two letters of favour
spread scatters the letters of laid-on into a new order

explanation.surface: Seek favour by offering a lavish feast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curry favour' looks like one idiom, but 'Curry' alone is the definition. 'spread' rearranges LAIDON into INDALO, held by VO.
explanation.definitionFit: A vindaloo is a hot Indian curry dish of Goan origin.

clue.text: YMCA's makeshift metal US plane

indicators.note: makeshift signals that the letters are put together in an improvised order

parts.note: ore is rock containing metal

explanation.surface: A youth hostel's improvised metal American aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' is the tree, not an aircraft; the S of YMCA's is part of the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: In America the plane tree is called a sycamore.

clue.text: Where material suitable for analysis surfaces? Wishful thinking

definitions.text: Where material suitable for analysis surfaces?
definitions.meaning: psychoanalysts study what comes up while we sleep and imagine
a retort that something hoped for will never happen

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading points to Freudian dream analysis.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a scornful retort meaning that what someone hopes for is pure fantasy.

clue.text: See 24
Artist accepted grand home briefly

parts.note: in means accepted or fashionable
G is short for grand, a thousand
res is short for residence, a home

explanation.surface: A painter is welcomed into a fine home for a short time.
explanation.walkthrough: Ingres was a French Neoclassical painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres was a celebrated French painter, an example of an artist.

clue.text: Daffy duck waddles at a funeral pace

indicators.note: Daffy means crazy, so these letters go crazily into a new order

parts.note: a duck is a zero in cricket, the letter O

explanation.surface: A cartoon duck waddles slowly along at a funeral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daffy duck' looks like the cartoon name, but Daffy is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a ship's order for the slowest possible speed, apt for a funeral procession.

clue.text: 20 is taken aback on entering

parts.note: the answer to 20, the French painter

indicators.note: taken aback means turned backwards, so is is reversed

explanation.surface: A painter is startled on coming in.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingression is the act of going in, so it means entering as a noun.

clue.text: It spins or turns to right

indicators.note: turns means that or is reversed

explanation.surface: Something twirls or goes round to the right.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is the rotating part of a machine, such as helicopter blades.

clue.text: Unabridged version of 1957 rock 'n' roll classic? Don't count on it

definitions.text: Unabridged version of 1957 rock 'n' roll classic?
definitions.meaning: Buddy Holly's 1957 hit title with its contraction spelled out in full
a scornful expression ... something will never happen

explanation.walkthrough: Buddy Holly and the Crickets' song title contracts 'will' to 'll; unabridged, the contraction is expanded.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a retort meaning that something is extremely unlikely to happen.

clue.text: Brave type of international joining football team almost

parts.note: a Lion is a player for the British and Irish Lions, a rugby international

indicators.note: almost removes the final letter of the team's name

parts.note: Hearts, Heart of Midlothian, is an Edinburgh football club

explanation.surface: A courageous type of international player joins a football side, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: Hearts is a Scottish football club; the Lions are the British and Irish rugby touring side.
explanation.definitionFit: A lionheart is a very courageous person, as in Richard the Lionheart.

clue.text: Chief law maker ultimately

parts.note: a rule is a law or regulation

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of maker

explanation.surface: The head of state is the one who makes the laws in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruler is a leader or head, i.e. the chief.

clue.text: For all to see (about time, too)

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the word for too goes around the letter for time

parts.note: overly means too, excessively

explanation.surface: Done in full view, and not before time either.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket looks like an aside, but it holds the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtly means openly, in a way that everyone can see.

clue.text: Inexperience wears off: name gained success finally

indicators.note: gained means the rearranged letters take in the letter for name
off means going wrong, so the letters of wears are rearranged
finally means the last letter of success

explanation.surface: Greenness fades once you gain a reputation and success at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges WEARS into RAWES, which takes in N; then S is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Rawness means a lack of experience, like being raw or green.
